title: Hotspot isolation and deferred-burst scheduling for hosted GPU capacity events
creator: Priya Sharma
description: Summary: Following the Jan 2025 hosted API capacity event where a small set of user traffic created persistent GPU hotspots and drove queue amplification, we will implement a two-pronged mitigation: (1) hotspot isolation via tenant-aware packing and soft eviction, and (2) a deferred-burst scheduling layer that intentionally buffers low-priority bursts for a short window rather than immediately inflating GPU allocations. Goals: reduce tail latency during multi-tenant hotspots, lower unnecessary scale-ups, and preserve SLOs for priority customers. This ticket captures design, implementation, rollout, and runbook updates.
work_items: Design tenant-aware packing heuristic: affinity score based on model, sequence length, and KV cache reuse
Implement soft eviction: graceful preemption of lower-priority requests with synthetic partial responses and auto-retry hints
Build deferred-burst scheduler: short-term buffer (50-500ms) + backpressure policy with SLA awareness
Metrics & alerting: new hotspot_score metric, deferred_burst_queue_length, and eviction_rate; wire to console dashboards and on-call alerts
E2E tests: synthetic hotspot generator, chaos test that simulates burst traffic from 10 tenants
Runbook & postmortem updates: add decision tree for enabling deferred-burst and steps to revert packing heuristics
design_decisions: Prefer soft eviction with retry hints over hard aborts to decrease client errors while regaining capacity
Buffer window set conservatively to 200ms by default based on observed median inter-arrival times — tunable via config
Tenant-aware packing uses a lightweight affinity score to avoid expensive global scheduling decisions in the hot path
Defer full autoscale triggers when hotspot_score is above threshold; allow local node draining first to avoid cluster-wide churn
tradeoffs: Buffering increases median latency for buffered requests by ~50-200ms but reduces tail latency and prevents large scale-ups
Soft eviction adds complexity in client retry semantics and requires SDK guidance; temporary partial responses might complicate some integrations
Affinity packing reduces global utilization slightly (1-3%) to gain predictability and lower cross-tenant interference
implementation_notes: PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1284 implements affinity score and packing changes
PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1297 adds deferred-burst queue and admission controller
Feature flag: runtime.hotspot_isolation.v2 behind enterprise-only flag for initial canary
Local test harness: tools/hotspot-sim/ with scripts to replay production traces (s3://redwood-prod-traces/hotspot-2025-01)
testing_plan: Unit tests for affinity scoring and packing behavior
Integration tests that assert node-level drain can prevent autoscale trigger for a 30s sustained burst
Performance bench: measure 95/99/999 latencies with and without deferred-burst using CI cluster
Chaos test: kill and restart a node under hotspot conditions to validate graceful soft eviction and request recovery
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): enable feature flag in staging and 2% of hosted partition; monitor hotspot_score, autoscale frequency, and SLOs
Phase 1 (limited): enable for low-risk customers and dedicated partitions for 24h, collect SDK feedback and edge cases
Phase 2 (gradual): 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 3 days with automated rollback on sustained error rate increase or SLO degradation
Fallback: feature flag off or reduce hotspot_buffer_ms to 50ms; add manual override to disable soft eviction per-tenant
alerts_and_dashboards: Console dashboard: Hotspot Overview (hotspot_score heatmap, deferred_burst_queue_length, eviction_rate)
Alert: hotspot_score > 0.9 for 60s in >3 nodes => P1 oncall notification
Alert: autoscale_count spikes by >2x in 5m correlated with hotspot_score => runbook stage: investigate packing and review recent model rollouts
SLO monitors: 99th percentile latency and error budget burn rate with tags per-priority-class
runbook_updates: Add section: "Hotspot isolation triage", steps to identify offending tenants via hotspot_score and traffic profiles
Add section: "Enable deferred-burst", safe parameter ranges and how to tune hotspot_buffer_ms based on observed inter-arrival times
Postmortem checklist: list of signals that justify immediate rollback and metrics to collect for RCA
stakeholder_feedback: PM (Maya Chen): requested strong guardrails to prevent accidental global rollout; suggested enterprise-only flag at first
Design (Lena Park): asked for clearer SDK messaging for soft eviction and partial responses; proposed standardized retry headers
SRE (Omar Hassan): emphasized need for deterministic eviction metrics and for making hotspot_score reproducible across nodes
Sales (Eliot Brooks): asked for a customer-facing changelog entry highlighting improved reliability for bursty workloads
open_risks: SDK adoption: clients may not react appropriately to partial responses; we need to publish SDK guidance and integrate retries
Measurement drift: hotspot_score calibration might need re-tuning across regions and model families
Edge cases: long-running KV-heavy sessions might be penalized by packing heuristics if not accounted for
